links.comparator_used: Status quo: the most accurate AI operating point (sensitivity/specificity 93.3%/87.7%), among 1100 simulated sensitivity/specificity pairs
links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness (ICER) of annual AI-based DR screening over 30 years
links.effect: Compared with the status quo, six scenarios were cost-saving and seven were cost-effective. The most cost-effective model had sensitivity 96.3% and specificity 80.4%. Cost-saving or cost-effective results needed minimum sensitivity of 88.2% and specificity of 80.4%. Higher DR prevalence and higher willingness-to-pay required higher sensitivity for optimal cost-effectiveness.
links.tradeoff: The cost-optimal operating point had lower specificity (80.4% vs 87.7%), which means more unnecessary referrals and possibly higher medical costs.
links.quote: The most cost-effective AI model exhibited higher sensitivity (96.3%) and lower specificity (80.4%) than the status quo.

design_hint: alert threshold selection (sensitivity/specificity operating point chosen by cost-effectiveness)
